claims.text: Eleven countries lie wholly or partly in the Nile basin: Burundi, DR Congo, Egypt, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania and Uganda.
vo: how many countries share the nile basin

claims.text: The river system runs from Lake Victoria (White Nile outlet at Jinja) north to the Mediterranean Sea.
vo: from lake victoria to the mediterranean

claims.text: The Nile is about 6,650 km (4,132 mi) long — the longest river in Africa (Britannica calls it the longest in the world; the Amazon claim is contested, so the script says 'in Africa').
vo: about six thousand six hundred and fifty kilometres

claims.text: The White Nile (from the Equatorial lakes) and the Blue Nile (from Lake Tana, Ethiopia) converge at Khartoum, Sudan.
vo: two rivers make it: the white nile from the lakes, the blue nile from ethiopia, meeting at khartoum

claims.text: The basin covers roughly a tenth of Africa (Wikipedia ≈ 2.93 million km² ≈ 10%; InfoNile 10.3%; Britannica drains ≈ 3,349,000 km²).
claims.note: kept for the record; not spoken or shown in v3 (Mercator satellite scene — no area claims, geolint P1)

claims.text: More than 300 million people rely on the waters of the Nile.
vo: more than three hundred million people rely on its water

claims.text: Border policy plates (the basin view shows three contested boundaries): Abyei is contested between Sudan and South Sudan and patrolled by UNISFA; the Ilemi Triangle is administered by Kenya and claimed by South Sudan; the Halaib Triangle is administered by Egypt and claimed by Sudan. No sovereignty asserted.

Hook framing: the Nile is popularly identified with Egypt (the downstream state, where it reaches the Mediterranean), but the basin is shared by eleven countries — the question's premise is the common misconception, not a factual assertion.
vo: think the nile is just egypt's river

myths.myth: The Nile flows through only Egypt and Sudan.
myths.reality: Its basin spans eleven countries; most of the water comes from the upstream states.

guardrails.why: Contested name — say 'the Gulf' or use both names (docs/BORDER_POLICY.md).
Sovereignty language on disputed areas is banned; say administers / claims.

landscape.our_gap: Feed versions read the number over stock footage; nobody lights the eleven states up one by one with the two Niles drawn on an equal-area map.
